nodes.title: A folder is any node with a children array

anchor.snippet: const isFolder = (node: FileNode): boolean => node.children !== undefined;

nodes.why: An empty folder has children: [] and must still open, close and show that it is empty.
nodes.alternative: Treat nodes with at least one child as folders.
nodes.tradeoff: Checking the length turns every empty folder into a file.

nodes.title: Sort folders first, then by name ignoring case
nodes.why: File explorers group folders above files, and README.md belongs between package.json and other files, not before them because of its capital letters.
nodes.tradeoff: Plain comparison puts every capitalized name before every lowercase one.

nodes.title: Flatten only the items that are visible
nodes.why: Keyboard movement walks the visible rows in order, so a flat list of what is on screen makes ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End one-line lookups.
nodes.alternative: Query the DOM for the next treeitem on every key press.
nodes.tradeoff: DOM queries work but couple the logic to markup; the flat list is also easy to test.

nodes.title: Keep the tab stop on a visible item
nodes.why: When a collapse hides the active item, its nearest visible ancestor takes the tab stop, so Tab still reaches the tree.
nodes.alternative: Store the tab stop and update it in every handler that can hide items.
nodes.tradeoff: Deriving it during render covers Collapse all, clicks and keys with one rule.

nodes.title: Move focus and the tab stop together
nodes.why: Roving tabindex means the focused item is also the only item with tabIndex 0.
nodes.alternative: Use aria-activedescendant and keep focus on the list.
nodes.tradeoff: Active-descendant avoids moving focus but is less reliable across screen readers.

nodes.title: Read the key from the item that has focus
nodes.why: One keydown handler on the tree serves every item; the event target tells which item the user is on.
nodes.alternative: Attach a handler to every item.
nodes.tradeoff: Per-item handlers multiply closures and bubble into ancestors anyway.

nodes.title: Right opens, then enters; Left closes, then climbs

anchor.snippet: else if (open && next && next.parentId === item.node.id) focusItem(next.node.id);

nodes.why: This is the tree view keyboard pattern: a second ArrowRight moves into the first child, and ArrowLeft on a closed item goes to its parent.
nodes.tradeoff: Users then need ArrowDown to enter a folder, which breaks the expected pattern.

nodes.title: aria-expanded on folders, aria-selected on files
nodes.why: Assistive technology announces expandable items from aria-expanded, so files must not carry it.
nodes.tradeoff: Files would be announced as collapsed folders.

nodes.title: Handle clicks on the row, not on the list item
nodes.why: List items nest, so a click handler on the li would also fire for every ancestor folder.
nodes.alternative: Stop propagation in an li click handler.
nodes.tradeoff: A row handler has nothing to stop and keeps the hit area obvious.

nodes.title: Render children only when the folder is open
nodes.why: Closed folders keep their children out of the DOM, so hidden items can never receive focus.
nodes.alternative: Render every level and hide closed ones with CSS.
nodes.tradeoff: Hidden but focusable items break keyboard order unless every one is also removed from the tab order.
